Good afternoon everyone. My name is Jim Newton and I'm speaking behalf of the Wentworth and Middle East Condominium Corporation, which represents 41 homeowners of single family homes at 501 Cartwright Street and the widows.
These 41 homes are all single family, stand alone houses at elsewhere in Saskatoon and now also in phase two of the widows are considered fee simple for municipal tax purposes.
Firstly, when the widows was originally developed, the city of Saskatoon designated the single family homes in Wentworth as barrel and condominium.
It's been a lot of discussion over the past three years regarding phase two of dreams development plan.

When our residents began hearing of the proposal for phase two to have single family homes designated as fee simple, our board received a number of questions as how the city could possibly approve fee simple in phase two when our homes in the same neighborhood are designated as barrel and condominium.
Homeowners in Wentworth are tax based on property value similar to other single family homes in Saskatoon and now also other single family homes in the widows that are fee simple.
The difference is that homeowners in Wentworth are financially responsible for the maintenance, renewal and replacement of all of our own infrastructure including sewer and water systems.
Street asphalt, maintenance and replacements of the street asphalt street cleaning, snow removal, fire hydrant, street lights etc.
The condominium property act of Saskatchewan requires all condominiums to maintain a reserve fund.

The last reserve fund study for Wentworth determined the residents must contribute and accumulate significant funds on an annual basis to ensure the long term sustainability of our infrastructure assets and to cover large unforeseen expenditures such as an underground sewer or water main break.
The major question has been posed by residents to the Wentworth board is why are we required to pay full city taxes and still have to contribute funds on an annual basis towards the maintenance.
The pair along term replacement of our infrastructure when other similar homeowners in Saskatoon do not.
The residents of Saskatoon are the residents of Wentworth are being taxed and thus charged twice for these items once by the city of Saskatoon and again by Wentworth condo corp.
Other owners of similar homes do not have to take on the financial burden of bearing these costs twice.
This is neither fair appropriate nor is it equitable to the residents of Wentworth at the Willows.
I suspect that members of the city council and the standing policy committee on finance would not want to pay taxes on infrastructure and services they are already required to pay for.
Now the single family homes in phase two of the Willows have been approved as fee simple by the city of Saskatoon Wentworth homeowners are being even further disadvantaged.
Phase two homeowners will receive full city services for their taxes while Wentworth homeowners only receive waste and recycling collection while also paying full city taxes in the city neighborhood.
This has the potential to negatively impact property values for Wentworth residents.

If you think about it why would prospective buyers purchase and Wentworth or they have to pay full taxes and additionally pay condo fees for services and infrastructure when just down the street and phase two.
Those costs and financial liabilities are covered by city taxes alone.

In addition to the above Wentworth residents also pay water service charges, charges, sewer infrastructure charges, infrastructure charges and store management charges on our monthly utility statements from the city of Saskatoon.
